title: Calibration orchestration: executor-wallet delegation, ephemeral artifact escrow, and accuracy rollback policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce an orchestration pattern for calibration runs that supports delegated executor wallets (scoped credentials for runners), ephemeral artifact escrow (time-bound encrypted snapshots), and an automated accuracy-rollback policy that can revert promoted quant profiles when validation gates fail.
background: Calibration runs for FP8/INT8 produce many intermediate artifacts (checkpoints, activation statistics, quant profiles). Customers with strict privacy and compliance needs require time-limited exposure and fine-grained delegation so partners or CI systems can execute runs without broad tenant-level keys. Additionally, we need a robust governance flow: promoted quant assets should be automatically rolled back if post-promote accuracy regressions are detected in production canaries.
proposed_solution: 1) Executor wallets: mint short-lived, scope-limited credentials tied to a single calibration run or agent; wallets grant minimal permissions (upload artifacts to escrow, update run status, attach metrics). 2) Ephemeral artifact escrow: artifacts from calibration runs are automatically encrypted and moved to an escrow store with TTLs; access requires the wallet and an audit check; artifacts older than TTL are purged or archived to customer-controlled storage. 3) Accuracy rollback policy: introduce a validation pipeline that runs against canaries after profile promotion; if accuracy drop exceeds configurable thresholds, trigger automated rollback to previous active profile and create an alert/incident with details. 4) Console UX: new run execution modal to choose executor wallet or default agent, TTL slider for artifacts, and a promotions page that surfaces pending rollback protections and simulation results.
acceptance_criteria: Executor wallets can be issued from Console or API with scoping to a single run and expiry between 1h-30d
Calibration run artifacts are stored encrypted in escrow with a configurable TTL per run and are inaccessible after expiry without an explicit restore workflow
Promote flow includes a post-promote validation stage that executes canary prompts and computes accuracy delta against baseline
If accuracy delta > configured threshold, system automatically rolls back to previous quant profile and opens a rollback ticket with links to artifacts and metrics
Audit logs capture wallet issuance, artifact access events, promotion/rollback events, and are queryable from Console logs page
End-to-end integration tests for wallet-limited runner, escrow TTL enforcement, and automated rollback exist in CI
tasks: Spec: executor wallet schema, permission model, UI layout for wallet issuance
Backend: wallet minting service, IAM bindings, API endpoints for run-scoped tokens
Storage: escrow bucket lifecycle policy, server-side encryption keys, access middleware that enforces wallet scope and TTL
Workflow: implement post-promotion validation job runner, threshold config, and rollback orchestrator
Console: run creation modal changes, artifact browser TTL column, promotions page with rollbacks and simulation results
Observability: add audit events, dashboard tiles for rollback frequency and artifact TTL expirations
Security review and privacy assessment with Legal for escrow retention defaults
E2E tests and staging rollout with a subset of beta customers
notes: We must avoid broad-scoped long-lived keys for CI integrations; executor wallets are the minimal-scope alternative.
Escrow TTL default should be conservative (30 days) but configurable per-organization and overridable per-run only by admins.
Rollback should be conservative: require two consecutive failing canary snapshots or an explicit override from SRE within 1 hour to avoid flapping profiles.
